Theme

Latin word

jūdicium

jūdicium, jūdiciī n.

noun, second declension

a judgement, an assessment; a court of justice; the trial held in it; judgement, a considered opinion; a trial

In this lexicon

  • assessment

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Q. Fr. 1.1.43: existimātiōnibus ac jūdiciīs

  • court

    the recommended word · classical · Nep. Epam. 8.2: in jūdicium vēnit; Quint. 4.2.25 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 194; Traupman 298; Traupman 335

  • opinion

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.1.4: meō jūdiciō; Traupman 354; Traupman 335

  • trial

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Caec. 6; Traupman 197

Examples

  • nōn est tibi hīs sōlīs ūtendum existimātiōnibus ac jūdiciīs quī nunc sunt hominum, sed iīs etiam quī futūrī sunt

    you must not rely only on the judgements and assessments of the people living now, but also on those of the people to comeCic. Q. Fr. 1.1.43
